contract: construct(instance) -> array of shape (n, 3): Cartesian coordinates of n atoms in reduced units (lattice constant 1). instance = {'potential': 'sutton_chen', 'kind': '12-6' | '9-6' | '10-8', 'n': atoms, 'n_exp', 'm_exp', 'c'}; called once for each of six instances (kind, n) = (12-6, 38), (12-6, 75), (9-6, 59), (9-6, 80), (10-8, 55), (10-8, 79); all calls together within 300 s (enforced) and should use at most 4 threads (not enforced by the evaluator). The evaluator recomputes E = sum_i [1/2 sum_{j!=i} r_ij^-n_exp - c sqrt(sum_{j!=i} r_ij^-m_exp)] over all pairs (no cutoff) with (n_exp, m_exp, c) = (12, 6, 144.41), (9, 6, 39.432), (10, 8, 34.408); atoms must be at least 0.35 apart. Score: mean over instances of 100*(E - E_pub)/|E_pub| against the putative global minima tabulated by Doye and Wales (1998) (minimize; 0 matches all six, negative is lower). chem_clusters.relax(positions, 'sutton_chen', kind) and chem_clusters.sutton_chen_energy_gradient(positions, kind) may be called
notes: Many-body Sutton-Chen energy recomputed without cutoff. Reference check (tests/test_chem_clusters.py): relaxed icosahedra and truncated octahedra reproduce nine published minima of all three parameter sets (n = 13, 38, 55, 79) within the four published decimals. Sizes for which Lopez-Castro et al. (2024) report lower energies than the database (12-6 n = 68, 10-8 n = 58) or failed to reproduce it (10-8 n = 60) are not used.

name: Sutton-Chen transition-metal cluster global minima
description: Find the lowest-energy structures of 38- to 80-atom clusters of the Sutton-Chen many-body metal potential with the silver, nickel and gold parameter sets (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye and Wales.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Doye and Wales (1998): Sutton-Chen 12-6, 9-6 and 10-8 clusters, table of putative global minima for N <= 80 (arXiv cond-mat/9711038).
Sutton and Chen (1990): the long-range Finnis-Sinclair potential and its (n, m, c) parameters.
Lopez-Castro, Ortiz-Chi and Merino (2024): GrowPAL search over Sutton-Chen clusters with 5-80 atoms; reports new lower minima for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58 (not used here).
LaTeX source of the global-minimum table (four decimals).

limitations: References are the 1998 putative minima (four decimals); the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24, and its coordinate files score them with this evaluator within 5e-5. Lopez-Castro et al. (2024) report database-level minima for all sizes from 5 to 80 except three (lower energies for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58, not reproduced for 10-8 N = 60); those three are excluded.
Putative minima are public, so remembered structures score well without search; the energy is computed without a cutoff, as in the source, and differs from implementations that truncate the sums.
The score averages relative energy excesses over six instances within a shared 300 s budget.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the lowest-energy structure of an atomic cluster for a given interatomic potential (global optimisation on a rugged energy landscape). Here: transition-metal clusters described by the many-body Sutton-Chen potential.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The structures of small metal clusters control catalytic, optical and magnetic properties of nanoparticles; many-body metal potentials give energy landscapes in which global optimisation still finds improvements decades later.

papers.task_relation: The task scores six of the tabulated sizes against those putative minima.
